title: Devolution without federalization
primary_topics: Quiet accomplishment of devolution's substantive goals without the disruption, expense, and contentiousness of federalist Charter change
President Duterte's notable omission of federalism -- his 2016 battle cry -- from his final State of the Nation Address
The 27.61 percent / P234.39 billion increase in LGU funding for 2022 (P848.5B → P1.083T) flowing from three legal gems acting in concert
Mandanas v. Ochoa (July 3, 2018) redefinition of LGU 'just share' to include tariff and customs duties, VAT, excise taxes, and natural-resource taxes (not just internal revenue)
Executive Order No. 138 (June 1, 2021) operationalizing function-and-service devolution alongside the funding shift
Three-branch institutional cooperation (Supreme Court + President + Congress) as the model of cadenced reform without Charter change
sub_topics: P1.083 trillion LGU release is about 20% of the P5 trillion 2022 proposed Executive budget
LGU revenues from Mandanas-broadened just share are additional to Local Government Code-authorized local taxes

EO 138 principle: 'public services with little or no benefit spillover are best administered and financed by lower level governments, while public services with significant inter-jurisdictional externalities or benefit and cost spillovers are best assigned to higher levels of government'
Department secretaries and agency heads directed to conduct functional and organizational reviews of their mandates
Preparation of 'devolution transition plans' (DTPs) by NG agencies
Establishment of the Growth Equalization Fund (GEF) to address marginalization, unequal development, and high poverty incidence among 'poor, disadvantaged and lagging LGUs'
Creation of the Committee on Devolution (ComDev) to oversee and monitor administrative and fiscal decentralization
LGU capacity-building; strengthening of planning, investment programming, budgeting linkage, and monitoring and evaluation systems
Reemployment options for adversely affected NG personnel: transfer within Executive branch without reduction in pay, or retirement benefits plus reapplication to LGUs as new employees
Constitutional mandate of decentralization (Art. X) as the throughline tying Mandanas, EO 138, and the LGC together

stances.claim: Federalism's avowed goal of devolution has been quietly accomplished without the contentious, costly Charter change long advocated by Duterte's 2016 campaign — explaining why federalism was absent from his final SONA.
stances.rhetorical_move: outcome-vindicates-quiet-reform: argues that means-of-reform matter and the substantive end was reached by less disruptive means
stances.evidence: Duterte's SONA omission; the P234.39B / 27.61% LGU funding jump from 2021 to 2022; convergent action by SC, President, and Congress

stances.claim: Three legal gems (Mandanas v. Ochoa, EO 138, and the Local Government Code) together constitute the operational backbone of Philippine devolution — a model of three-branch institutional cooperation.
stances.rhetorical_move: synthetic-framework: names and integrates three instruments under a single explanatory schema
stances.evidence: Mandanas's expansion of 'just share' to include customs, VAT, excise, natural-resource taxes; EO 138's functional-review and DTP architecture; LGC's pre-existing local-tax authority

stances.claim: EO 138's spillover principle ('benefit-spillover-determines-jurisdictional-assignment') provides a sound, technocratic basis for allocating responsibilities across NG and LGU levels.
stances.evidence: Direct quotation of EO 138 spillover language; integration with capacity-building and GEF safeguards

stances.claim: The Growth Equalization Fund and the Committee on Devolution provide necessary safeguards against the equity risks of decentralization (marginalization, unequal development, high poverty incidence in lagging LGUs).
stances.evidence: GEF and ComDev mandates as enumerated in EO 138

notable_anecdotes: Duterte's 2016 federalism battle cry going unmentioned in his final SONA — used as the column's opening puzzle and its rhetorical answer: substantive devolution was achieved without Charter change.

The specific P848.5B-to-P1.083T LGU jump (27.61% / P234.39B more) framed as a delight to 'provincial governors, city and town mayors, and barangay captains' — converting abstract devolution into a concrete fiscal windfall.

EO 138's pragmatic personnel-transition option (transfer without pay reduction, or retirement plus reapplication to LGUs as new employees) presented as an empathetic safeguard for adversely affected NG workers.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with a puzzle -- President Duterte's notable omission of federalism, his 2016 campaign battle cry, from his final SONA -- and answers it by arguing that federalism's avowed goal of devolution has been quietly accomplished without a tedious, disruptive, expensive, and much-ballyhooed Charter change. Starting in 2022, LGUs will automatically receive 27.61 percent more (P234.39 billion more, from P848.5 billion to P1.083 trillion -- about 20 percent of the P5 trillion 2022 Executive budget proposal) from the National Government, plus broader powers and functions. He identifies 'three legal gems' as the operational backbone: Mandanas v. Ochoa (July 3, 2018) ruling that the LGUs' 'just share' under the Constitution should include not only national internal revenue tax collections but also tariff and customs duties, VAT (in certain areas), excise taxes, and natural-resource taxes; Executive Order No. 138 (June 1, 2021) operationalizing the principle that 'public services with little or no benefit spillover are best administered and financed by lower level governments, while public services with significant inter-jurisdictional externalities or benefit and cost spillovers are best assigned to higher levels of government,' with directives for department secretaries to conduct functional-organizational reviews, prepare devolution transition plans, build LGU capacity, strengthen planning-investment-budgeting linkages, develop communication strategies, and establish the Growth Equalization Fund (GEF) and the Committee on Devolution (ComDev); and the Local Government Code which already authorizes LGUs to impose and collect local taxes on top of the Mandanas-broadened just share. EO 138 also gives adversely affected NG personnel reemployment options (transfer within the Executive branch without pay reduction, or retirement benefits plus reapplication to LGUs as new employees). He concludes by celebrating the three-branch institutional cooperation -- Supreme Court (Mandanas), President (EO 138), and Congress (Local Government Code) -- that delivered substantive devolution without a contentious Charter change and without adding a new, costly, and burdensome layer of governance.
